## Summary

George: "I thought prompt engineering is dead, but the amount of miles I get out of this prompt just blows my mind. It's particularly surprising because it is very plain language with no jargon whatsoever."

The prompt itself (photo in the quoted tweet, verbatim):

> A simple prompt that often helps me: I want a deeper version of this task, not a bigger one. Before rewriting it: (1) say what a top professional in this field would do here that I'm not asking for; (2) name the rawest material they would start from instead of what has already been digested for me; (3) name the specific methods and tools they would use; (4) say what, other than you or me, would show the result is right. Then rewrite my prompt to ask for exactly that.

**Share chain:** George (2026-10-19) ← Sar Haribakti (@sarthakgh, 2026-10-14, "A prompt to come up with a better prompt" + the photo) ← Felix Rieseberg (@felixrieseberg, Claude eng lead) announcing a tutorial on "being more ambitious" with AI — tutorial link 404 at capture, so the prompt's original authorship is unverified (likely the tutorial, possibly sarthakgh's own recipe).

The move: before executing a task, make the agent elicit the *expert's* version of the task — scope you didn't ask for (1), rawer inputs (2), real methods/tools (3), an external check (4) — then rewrite the ask to target that. Depth through better specification, not more volume.

## Why it matters

- **The sibling of Agrawal's compression prompts** ([[2026-09-17-agrawal-agent-simplification-prompts]]): his "much simpler solution, 80% of benefits" pass compresses the *solution* after planning; this compresses-and-deepens the *task* before execution. Same economics — the default failure is bigness (more features, more scope) when what pays is sharpness.
- **Q4 is verifiers-first in one sentence** — "what, other than you or me, would show the result is right" is exactly [[2026-09-14-rauchg-verifiers-skills-new-frameworks]]: an external check beats self-report. A task spec that demands its own falsification channel is stronger than any instruction to "be accurate".
- **Q2 is a brain-rot defense** — "the rawest material instead of what has already been digested for me" is the same muscle as Socratic AI over answer AI ([[2026-10-18-thomwolf-avoid-brain-rot]]): route work through primaries, not pre-digested feeds.
- **Slots into the planning loop** ([[2026-09-06-phelps-agentic-planning-loop]]): run this rewrite pass on the PRD/task before the critique loop — better question in, better plan out. Prompts steer one output; where a rule must hold every time it graduates to a check ([[2026-09-06-julian-risk-based-code-review]]).
- **"Prompt engineering is dead" counterpoint:** the leverage was never jargon — it's task specification. Plain language that forces expert framing outperforms decorated prompts.
- **Directly adoptable here:** we produce research briefs and plans for the user (Concierge & Research lane). A standing "deeper version, not bigger" pass on the *ask* before dispatching research would raise every brief's floor.

**Skepticism gates:**
- "Blows my mind" is n=1 enthusiasm; 0 replies and no engagement stats at capture — no saved-as-recipe signal from the crowd yet.
